thread:
maria: Heads-up — planning a canary for model v3. The idea: percent-based ramp but cap request velocity per cohort. Want feedback on the policy shape and API fields.
lee: +1. Can you sketch what 'cap request velocity' looks like? Is that RPM per cohort or tokens/sec? :thinking_face:
maria: RPM per cohort initially, tokens/sec for global guard. Proposal: each step defines {percent, max_rpm, duration_s}. Example below.
maria: ```json
[ { "percent": 5, "max_rpm": 120, "duration_s": 1800 },
  { "percent": 20, "max_rpm": 480, "duration_s": 3600 },
  { "percent": 50, "max_rpm": 1200, "duration_s": 7200 } ]
```
sam: I like combining percent + rpm. Two concerns: 1) skew between small customers and big ones (percent of traffic might still flood small pools), 2) how do we enforce per-customer QoS? 
anya: For (1) we should add an absolute minimum and maximum per-cohort, so tiny cohorts don't get 0. Also per-customer limit as override: customers can opt-in to be excluded from canary or have dedicated cohort.
lee: Also add jitter to step transitions to avoid simultaneous switch storms across regions. E.g., step start = scheduled_start + rand(0, jitter_s).
maria: Good call. Add fields: "min_rpm_per_cohort", "max_rpm_per_cohort", "start_jitter_s". Any objections to exposing these in the Console UI vs API-only? 
sam: Console should show effective expected qps and a visual timeline. But API must be canonical source. Console just edits templated JSON and validates.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary v3 -> v2 swap; config id=canary-2765432100; expected finish ~ +3h :rocket:
lee: How do we validate guards? My proposal: each step has guard conditions (error_rate_pct < 0.5, median_latency_ms < 600, obs_quality_score delta < 0.02). If any guard trips, auto-fallback to previous stable and notify.
anya: Add "hold_on_fail": true and "escalation_channel": "#incidents". Also want an opt for manual gating per step (auto=false) for sensitive customers.
maria: What about A/B experiments? We need to separate 'canary' from 'experiment' mode — experiments should support weighted metrics and hypothesis IDs. Will the same config work? 
sam: Keep them distinct. Canary config focuses on safety (guards, rollbacks). Experiment config extends with sampling rules and metric buckets. But share common fields: percent, duration, start_jitter.
lee: One more: rate-limiter interactions. If global rate-limiter kicks in, canary percent should be recomputed downstream. We need a contract: percent is best-effort and is applied before quota enforcement; if quota trimming happens, we log "effective_percent" in telemetry.
maria: Telemetry fields we want in Console: requested_percent, effective_percent, max_rpm, step_state (running/held/failed), guard_tripped_reason, rollback_ts. These should be exported to tracing/metrics.
anya: UX: Console should render a quick-read status badge per model: green/amber/red + hover for details. And allow 'pause' and 'rollback' buttons inline.
sam: For API debate: json vs nested HCL-ish structure. I prefer JSON schema + server-side validation. It simplifies storage and patches.
lee: +1 for JSON schema. We should publish schema and sample configs in repo and Console will call validator endpoint on save.
maria: I'll draft a PR with JSON schema and a small UI mock. Will include the min/max/jitter and guard fields. Thanks all.
deploy-bot: update: canary step1 reached 5% (max_rpm enforced 118/120), effective_percent=5.0, region=us-west-2.
ops-staging: saw a small spike in 95p latency at t+600s, guard still green but monitoring closely. :eyes:
maria: noted — hold at step1 for another 10m and re-evaluate. I'll add a temporary hold flag.
lee: If we end up with repeated holds, consider decreasing step ramp (5->10->25 instead of 5->20) — we should make step profiles editable templates.
maria: Agreed, will add templates: conservative / default / aggressive.
anya: Can we also add a 'dry-run' mode where traffic is mirrored to v3 but not shifted? Useful for perf/telemetry baseline.
sam: Mirror mode is great for perf tests, but be mindful of cost. Make it opt-in per rollout.
maria: Cool — PR incoming. If anyone wants to review early, ping me.
